ThunderKittens bugs found by Volta
==================================

ThunderKittens at 67845f5f (2026-09-12), the submodule external/ptx/sources/ThunderKittens,
compiled for sm_100a (fftconv_non_pc for sm_90a) by external/ptx/extraction/thunderkittens.py.
Run them with `just kittens` (external/ptx/races.py --framework thunderkittens); verdicts are in
external/ptx/output/thunderkittens.csv.

TK-1 to TK-7 come from Volta runs of the educational GEMMs and the unit tests. TK-8 to TK-10
are in production kernels Volta cannot run (2-CTA clusters): TK-8 was found and checked with
SentryWard (~/Desktop/sentryward), TK-9 and TK-10 by reading the code.

Every bug below is a synchronization error: on the schedule Volta found, a thread overwrites,
re-initializes or frees something another thread can still be using. Each is "latent": the
warps usually stay converged and the asynchronous ops finish quickly, so the tests pass on
hardware, but the PTX memory model does not guarantee the order they rely on. For TK-2 to TK-7,
a fixed copy of the test (`FIXES` in extraction/thunderkittens.py, built into
thunderkittens/patched/) is race free and equal to its spec, which confirms the diagnosis.
TK-1 was confirmed independently with SentryWard.

Summary
-------
  TK-1  educational level_06: a lagging thread's parity wait can miss a phase (hang)   kernel
  TK-2  TMA load unit tests: smem and mbarrier reused with no __syncwarp                test
  TK-3  TMA store unit tests: only lane 0 waits for the TMA store to finish reading     test
  TK-4  tcgen05 unit test: every warp runs mbarrier.init on the same live mbarrier      test
  TK-5  managed tensor_allocator: warp 0 frees Tensor Memory other warps still read     library
  TK-6  tile TMA store test: store_async_read_wait<3> waits for too few stores          test
  TK-7  tcgen05 accumulate test: second MMA re-arms the mbarrier before every warp
        saw the first phase (hang)                                                      test
  TK-8  B300 attention: the corrector signals rescale_finished from one thread before
        its other warps waited on corr_arrived (missed phase, hang)                     kernel
  TK-9  B300 causal attention, persistent: corrector warps read max_vec_smem after the
        signal that lets softmax overwrite it (wrong O and LSE)                         kernel
  TK-10 B200 GEMMs (bf16, fp8, int8): CTA 1 sends a remote mbarrier arrive into CTA 0's
        shared memory after CTA 0 may have exited                                       kernel


TK-1  level_06: parity aliasing on inputs_arrived (latent hang)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    kernels/gemm/educational_b200/level_06.cu (wait(inputs_arrived, phase), line 73)
Volta:    educational_b200/level_06.n128, .n256: CHECK-FAILED, barrier epochs (mbarrier phases)
          EpochViolation and mbarrier release order Unordered.
What:     Thread 0 re-arms inputs_arrived for phase k+1 (expect_bytes + TMA) as soon as it has
          passed phase k itself. The other 127 threads only ever wait on inputs_arrived, and
          nothing orders their wait for phase k before thread 0 arms phase k+1. If phase k+1
          completes before a lagging thread waits, its parity wait for k sees the parity it
          expects only after phase k+2, so it skips a phase or hangs.
Fix:      a named barrier of the 128 threads (bar.sync 2, 128) after each inputs_arrived wait.
Status:   confirmed with SentryWard (not_wellsynced; race_free once fixed, and Volta VERIFIED).
          Already volta_findings.txt (5).


TK-2  TMA load unit tests reuse shared memory and the mbarrier without a warp sync
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    tests/thread/memory/tile/tma.cu, test_load (lines 37-40) and test_load_oob (84-87);
          tests/thread/memory/vec/tma.cu, test_load (lines 31-33).
Volta:    units/thread_memory_tile_tma.test_load.bf16.1.1.1, units/thread_memory_vec_tma.
          test_load.bf16.1.1: CHECK-FAILED (EpochViolation on smem_semaphore, mbarrier release
          order), and REJECT against the identity spec: on the schedule Volta runs, the copy
          is refuted numerically.
What:     Each loop iteration is: lane 0 arms smem_semaphore and issues the TMA loads into
          shared_tile; the warp waits; every lane copies shared_tile out with warp::store. Then
          lane 0 starts the next iteration. warp::store ends with no __syncwarp, so lane 0 can
          issue the next TMA load into shared_tile while other lanes are still reading it (a
          generic read / async-proxy write race), and can re-arm smem_semaphore before they
          waited on the current phase (the TK-1 parity hazard).
Fix:      __syncwarp() at the end of each iteration, after the warp::store loop.
Status:   fixed tests (patched/thread_memory_tile_tma.test_load, patched/thread_memory_vec_tma.
          test_load) are RACE-FREE and ACCEPT.


TK-3  TMA store unit tests: only lane 0 waits for the TMA store to finish reading
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    tests/thread/memory/tile/tma.cu, test_store (lines 118-119);
          tests/thread/memory/vec/tma.cu, test_store (lines 57-60), and the reduce variants.
Volta:    units/thread_memory_tile_tma.test_store.bf16.1.1.1, units/thread_memory_vec_tma.
          test_store.bf16.1.1: RACE-CONDITION, MemoryConflict ReadWrite on Shared: the TMA
          store's read of the tile and a lane's warp::load write into it.
What:     `if(threadIdx.x == 0) store_async_read_wait()` is followed directly by every lane
          writing the next data into the same shared tile or vector. Only lane 0 has waited for
          the in-flight bulk store to finish reading it; lanes 1-31 can overwrite it first.
Fix:      __syncwarp() after lane 0's store_async_read_wait.
Status:   the fixed vector test is RACE-FREE and ACCEPT. The tile test also needs TK-6's fix.


TK-4  tcgen05 unit test: every warp initializes the same mbarrier
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    tests/group/mma/tensor/mma.cu, tcgen05_wrapper (line 85); the same line in
          tcgen05_nvfp4_k64_wrapper (line 383), read in the code (Volta does not run the
          block-scaled tests).
Volta:    units/group_mma_tensor_mma.bf16.st.mm_AB: RACE-CONDITION, MemoryConflict WriteWrite on
          Shared address 8 (the mbarrier `sem`).
What:     The kernel runs 4 warps (group<4>), and all of them call
          kittens::warp::init_semaphore(sem, 0, 1). That function executes mbarrier.init on
          lane 0 of each calling warp, so four mbarrier.init run on one object, unordered with
          each other. Re-initializing a live mbarrier without mbarrier.inval is undefined
          behavior (PTX ISA, mbarrier.init).
Fix:      `if(threadIdx.x == 0) kittens::init_semaphore(sem, 0, 1);` (the __syncthreads that
          follows already publishes it).
Status:   fixed test (patched/group_mma_tensor_mma.bf16.st.mm_AB, with TK-5's fix) is RACE-FREE
          and ACCEPT.


TK-5  managed tensor_allocator frees Tensor Memory other warps may still read
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    include/types/tensor/tensor.cuh, ~tensor_allocator (lines 150-157): for a 1-CTA
          allocator, warp 0 calls deprovision() (tcgen05.dealloc) at scope exit with no CTA
          barrier. Hit by tests/group/mma/tensor/mma.cu (tcgen05_wrapper ends with
          tcgen05.ld + G::store, line 146) and tests/group/memory/tile/tensor_to_register.cu
          (group_tensor_reg_load_store's f32/int path, line 68, and group_tensor_reg_lane_row).
Volta:    units/group_memory_tile_tensor_to_register.group_tensor_reg_load_store.f32.8.2.4.row
          (CHECK-FAILED) and units/group_mma_tensor_mma.bf16.st.mm_AB (beside TK-4's race):
          resource lifetime UseNotBeforeDeallocation, a warp's tcgen05.ld unordered with warp
          0's tcgen05.dealloc.
What:     Each warp reads its slice of Tensor Memory (tcgen05.ld, tcgen05.wait::ld) and stores
          it out. Warp 0 then leaves the allocator's scope and deallocates, possibly while warps
          1-3 are still reading. Kernels that end with a CTA-wide barrier after their last
          Tensor Memory access (educational levels 06-08) are unaffected. The destructor makes
          every user responsible for that barrier but does not say so; the 2-CTA path does
          synchronize, with a cluster barrier.
Fix:      in the tests, tensor_before_thread_sync(); __syncthreads(); before the scope ends. In
          the library, the managed destructor could fence and barrier the CTA (or document the
          requirement).
Status:   fixed tests (patched/group_memory_tile_tensor_to_register...f32.8.2.4.row,
          patched/group_mma_tensor_mma.*) are RACE-FREE and ACCEPT.


TK-6  tile TMA store test: store_async_read_wait<3> waits for too few stores
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    tests/thread/memory/tile/tma.cu, test_store (line 118).
Volta:    with TK-3 fixed, still RACE-CONDITION: MemoryConflict ReadWrite on Shared address 512,
          which is shared_tile[0][1].
What:     Each iteration stores 4 tiles (4 bulk groups), then the next iteration loads into
          tile [i][j] after store_async_read_wait<3>() (at most 3 groups still reading). No
          store is issued between the four loads. Before tile [0][0] the wait retires the oldest
          group, tile [0][0]'s store, which is correct. Before tiles [0][1], [1][0] and [1][1]
          the 3 pending groups are exactly those tiles' stores, so the wait returns at once
          and the warp overwrites tiles their TMA stores may still be reading. The comment
          "make sure next tile is ready for write" holds only for the first tile.
Fix:      store_async_read_wait<3 - (2*i + j)>, or store_async_read_wait<0> once before the
          loads (the fix used).
Status:   fixed test (patched/thread_memory_tile_tma.test_store.bf16.1.1.1, with TK-3) is
          RACE-FREE and ACCEPT.


TK-7  tcgen05 accumulate test: second MMA re-arms the mbarrier too early (latent hang)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Where:    tests/group/mma/tensor/mma.cu, tcgen05_wrapper ACC paths (lines 117-118, 133-134).
Volta:    with TK-4 and TK-5 fixed, units/group_mma_tensor_mma.bf16.st.mma2_AB is still
          CHECK-FAILED: barrier epochs (mbarrier phases) EpochViolation on `sem`.
What:     `run_mma(..., sem); wait(sem, 0); run_mma(..., sem); wait(sem, 1);`, executed by all
          128 threads. The issuing thread starts the second MMA, whose commit completes phase 1
          of sem, as soon as it has passed wait(sem, 0) itself. If phase 1 completes before a
          lagging warp reaches wait(sem, 0), that warp sees parity 0 again and waits for a
          third phase that never comes: the same parity aliasing as TK-1.
Fix:      __syncthreads() between wait(sem, 0) and the second run_mma.
Status:   fixed test (patched/group_mma_tensor_mma.bf16.st.mma2_AB) is RACE-FREE and ACCEPT.


TK-8  B300 attention: rescale_finished signalled before every corrector warp waited
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Issue:    https://github.com/HazyResearch/ThunderKittens/issues/222 (opened 2026-11-27, [WIP])
Where:    kernels/attention/bf16_b300_mha_causal/bf16_b300_mha_causal.cu, persistent path lines
          434-437 (task start) and 478-481 (final normalization), one-task path 541-544 and
          586-588; kernels/attention/bf16_b300_mha_noncausal/bf16_b300_mha_noncausal.cu lines
          280-283 and 325-327. Every variant of both kernels.
What:     corr_arrived[q] (count 4: one arrival per softmax warp) is waited by all 4 corrector
          warps; then warpgroup::arrive(rescale_finished[q]) arrives from the warpgroup's lane 0
          only (mbarrier.arrive.release.cta), with no warpgroup::sync between the two. The
          softmax warpgroup's next corr_arrived arrival waits only on rescale_finished, so it is
          ordered after warp 0's wait but not after warps 1-3's. A lagging corrector warp can
          find corr_arrived two phases ahead, wait on the aliased parity, and from then on run
          one phase behind its warpgroup (it skips a phase, then blocks or desynchronizes the
          warpgroup's named barriers). The in-loop arrives (causal line 472, non-causal 318)
          already have the warpgroup::sync and are correct.
Tools:    SentryWard on the causal persistent kernel (2-SM build, B = 1, S = 512, H = 2;
          representative branches for the data-dependent rescale): not_wellsynced,
          issue_not_ordered_before_next_phase: a corrector wait on corr_arrived not ordered
          before the 4 softmax warps' arrivals of the next phase (generation 1, lines 434-437).
          With a warpgroup::sync added there only, the same failure moves to generation 5, the
          final normalization's wait (lines 478-481).
Fix:      warpgroup::sync(warpgroup::groupid()+1) before each of those warpgroup::arrive calls.
Status:   with every one of those arrives synchronized, SentryWard's synchronization check passes
          (B = 1, S = 512, H = 1; its memory check stops at an unresolved Tensor Memory alias,
          unsupported). The unfixed kernel fails at that size in about 2 minutes.

TK-9  B300 causal attention (persistent): max_vec_smem read after the release that frees it
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Issue:    https://github.com/HazyResearch/ThunderKittens/issues/223 (opened 2026-11-27, [WIP])
Where:    bf16_b300_mha_causal.cu lines 478-481 (corrector) against line 713 (softmax).
What:     In the final normalization, all 128 corrector threads read row_sum from
          max_vec_smem[q][lane] (line 479), then lane 0 alone arrives on rescale_finished (481).
          Softmax warpgroup 0 of CTA 0 starts its next task by waiting on rescale_finished, and
          at idx == 0 with m_tile == 0 (t_coord.y == 0) it writes acc_scale into the same
          max_vec_smem[0][lane] (line 713). The non-causal kernel guards this write with idx > 0.
          Nothing orders corrector warps 1-3's reads before that write. A lagging warp reads
          acc_scale (0 on the first block) instead of the row sum: rows 32-127 of the tile are
          stored unnormalized and their LSE is -inf, silently. It needs a CTA whose second or
          later task has t_coord.y == 0, which the persistent scheduler produces once B*H*S/256
          exceeds the 148 SMs (for example B*H = 16, S = 8192).
Tools:    found by reading the code. TK-8's fix (a warpgroup::sync before line 481) also orders
          these reads; SentryWard does not reach its memory check without TK-8's fix.
Fix:      warpgroup::sync before line 481 (TK-8), or guard line 713 with idx > 0 as the
          non-causal kernel does.

TK-10 B200 GEMMs: remote arrive into a CTA that may have exited
---------------------------------------------------------------
Issue:    https://github.com/HazyResearch/ThunderKittens/issues/224 (opened 2026-11-27, [WIP])
Where:    kernels/gemm/bf16_b200/bf16_b200_gemm.cu lines 137 (producer) and 151 (CLC warp); the
          same lines in fp8_b200 and int8_b200. Exit gate: lines 248-250.
What:     When the scheduler's response says no more work, CTA 1's producer and CLC warps
          still do tma::cluster::arrive(schedule_finished, 0), a remote mbarrier arrive into
          CTA 0's shared memory, and then exit. Nothing in CTA 0 waits for that phase: its CLC
          warp breaks out before waiting on schedule_finished again, and its only exit gate is
          tmem_finished, which CTA 1's epilogue signals, not its producer or CLC warp. So CTA 0
          can deallocate and exit while CTA 1's producer is still stalled before its arrive,
          which then writes into the shared memory of a CTA that has exited. The CUDA guide
          requires all distributed shared memory accesses to finish before a block exits; a
          cluster barrier at the end, or waiting on the last schedule_finished phase, fixes it.
          mxfp8_b200 and nvfp4_b200 have no CLC pipeline and are unaffected.
Tools:    found by reading the code. SentryWard verifies these kernels (all four configurations
          of each, at 1 and 10 K-steps) but does not model DSMEM accesses after a CTA's exit.

Plausible, not confirmed (production kernels, code reading)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- fp8_vr200 (and _fp8out): with M_TILE_COUNT = 1 and N_PAIR_COUNT = 4, which its static_asserts
  allow but its main() does not instantiate, MMA_PIPE_DEPTH is 2 while outputs_arrived is a
  single mbarrier: the MMA warp can commit two tasks ahead and the epilogue's parity wait
  aliases (deadlock). fp8_vr200_gemm.cu lines 29, 151, 206, 236, 259.
- nvfp4_vr200: CTA 1's last arrive on schedule_finished (lines 215-216, 288) may have the same
  exit hazard as TK-10; not traced.
- nvfp4_b200 (line 243), nvfp4_b300 (line 414) and fp8_vr200_fp8out (line 298) read the global
  scale factors before griddepcontrol.wait under PDL; only the loader warps wait. nvfp4_vr200
  calls pdl::wait in its consumer first (line 388).
- Most production kernels exit with TMA stores possibly still reading shared memory (no final
  store_async_read_wait<0>): the B200 GEMMs, nvfp4_b300, fp8_vr200, nvfp4_vr200 (bf16 out) and
  the B300 attention kernels. nvfp4_vr200_gemm_fp4out waits (line 519).
- Library-wide: warpgroup::load_async issues tcgen05.ld and the kernels use the registers
  before tcgen05.wait::ld; cross-warp Tensor Memory handoffs (alloc then use, ld then the next
  MMA's overwrite, use then dealloc) mostly lack tcgen05.fence::before/after_thread_sync.
  Formal violations of the PTX ISA that current hardware tolerates.

Rejected, but not ThunderKittens bugs
-------------------------------------
- educational_b200/level_07.n256 and level_08.n256: RACE-CONDITION, WriteWrite on Shared 1024
  (a_smem[0]) between the first and the fourth K-step's TMA load (4 K-steps over 3 stages).
  The program does order them: TMA load, then the inputs_arrived wait, the MMA that reads the
  stage, its tcgen05.commit on inputs_finished, and the producer's wait before the next load.
  Volta orders each step but does not carry the first load through the commit's completion.
  This is an open Volta modeling question (happens-before through tracked async ops,
  volta_findings.txt (a)), not a ThunderKittens race. Both are equal to their GEMM spec.
- 45 unit tests stop at a read of never-written local memory: the compiler copies a 16-byte
  aggregate of which 8 bytes were written and overwrites the rest before use. Volta aborts
  on any such read. This is a Volta gap, not undefined behavior that matters.

Not reached (Volta stops before a verdict)
------------------------------------------
- The B200 production GEMMs (bf16, fp8, int8, mxfp8, nvfp4), educational level_09 and the
  B300 attention kernels run as 2-CTA clusters (cta_group::2, .reqnctapercluster); Volta
  models one CTA per cluster.
- rotary: a register-named bar.sync whose thread count varies; layernorm: a generic
  (space-less) ld in curand's state.
- The H100 kernels (attention, mamba2, based, hedgehog, linear_attention, flux, fftconv_pc,
  educational_h100 levels 05-08) use wgmma, which Volta does not model.
- Unit tests: mma .satfinite (int8), tcgen05.st .16x128b, tcgen05.mma kind::i8, TMA reduce
  stores, multicast, a bf16x2 exp (packed pair) and fp8 cvt forms.
